# Lab Samples by Drone: Switzerland Was First, Now Others Are Flying

> In 2017 Switzerland was one of the first countries to authorise drone flights carrying lab samples over cities. Today London and Baden-Württemberg fly lab samples on a scheduled basis, and in Switzerland we cannot find a single route. What cantons can do as hospital owners.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/drohnen-fuer-spitaeler/ · Published: 2026-11-16 · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

In March 2017 the Federal Office of Civil Aviation (FOCA/BAZL) authorised Swiss Post and Matternet to make the first commercial drone flights beyond visual line of sight over cities. In Lugano, Bern and Zurich, drones carried lab samples between hospitals. After two crashes in 2019 and economic problems, Swiss Post pulled out in 2022. Today hospitals in London and Baden-Württemberg fly samples on a scheduled basis; for Switzerland we have found no evidence of regular operation. The rules exist. What is missing is a client, and that can be the cantons as owners of their hospitals.

<!-- more -->

---

## Methodology

The note is based on FOCA's pages, the Federal Council report "Development and regulation of civil drones in Switzerland" of 20 December 2024, the final report of the Swiss Transportation Safety Investigation Board (STSB/SUST) on the 2019 Zurich crash, and statements by operators and hospitals. There are no public statistics on current operations in Switzerland; our statement rests on the fact that no operator, hospital or authority reports a running hospital route for 2025 and 2026. Time and cost figures come from operators, hospitals and the press.

---

### The Swiss pioneer years

- **2017 Lugano:** Swiss Post, the Ticino hospital group EOC and Matternet fly samples between the Civico and Italiano hospitals, about 1,300 flights in the first year.
- **2018 Bern and Zurich:** samples from Tiefenau hospital to the Inselspital; across Lake Zurich from the Klinik Im Park to the central laboratory, 5.8 km in about 7 minutes.
- **2019, two crashes:** in January into Lake Zurich, in May in Zurich-Oberstrass, with no injuries. The STSB found weaknesses in the flight control and a severed parachute line. FOCA then required a parachute meeting the standard, lower speed and a new risk assessment.
- **2020 restart, 2022 exit:** according to Swiss Post, samples in Lugano arrived up to 45 minutes faster than by courier. In 2022 Swiss Post handed operations to Matternet because they were not profitable and technology and regulation did not allow wide use. At the end of 2022 Matternet tested a 5 km route between the Triemli and Waid city hospitals; we could not find evidence of permanent operation.

### How others do it today

- **London:** since autumn 2024 drones have flown samples between the Guy's and St Thomas' laboratories. Instead of more than half an hour by road, the flight takes under two minutes; by February 2026 more than 6,000 samples had been flown.
- **Baden-Württemberg:** since 2025 the Zollernalb Klinikum has flown lab samples over about 20 km of populated area. Seven flights a day cost about €75,000 a year; the previous vehicle transport cost €180,000 to €220,000.
- **Rwanda:** Zipline drones deliver blood products on average 79 minutes faster than by road; according to a study in The Lancet Global Health, expired blood units fell by an estimated 67%.

### What applies today

- **Rules:** since 1 January 2023 the EU drone rules have applied in Switzerland. Flights beyond visual line of sight need an operational authorisation from FOCA based on a risk assessment (SORA), or an operator certificate (LUC) that lets operators approve routes themselves. In 2024 Matternet was the first company to receive such a certificate for flights over populated areas.
- **Airspace:** the first U-space, an airspace with digital traffic management for drones, is planned for the Zurich area and is due to start at the end of 2026.
- **Cantons:** according to the Federal Council, landing sites count as very small structures, not as airfields. Cantons are responsible for spatial planning, building permits and noise assessment. And most hospitals belong to cantons or communes.

---

## What this means for policy

The Confederation authorises flights and airspace. But whether a route comes into being depends on who orders and pays for it, and for lab samples that is mostly public hospitals.

- **Order:** the canton includes drone transport for lab samples, blood and urgent medicines in its hospitals' service mandates and lab-logistics tenders, where it saves time or money.
- **Bundle:** one network for several hospitals and labs instead of single routes, so that one operator can apply for an authorisation covering a whole network.
- **Prepare:** clear landing sites on hospital roofs for planning and noise in advance, so that a route does not fail at the building permit.
- **Safety first:** only certified operators, parachutes meeting the standard and publicly reported incidents; the lessons of 2019 are a condition, not an obstacle.
- **Measure:** publish flights, time saved, costs and incidents every year, compared with couriers: [Life Science & Health](@/life-science.en.md).
- **Zurich as a start:** with the Zurich U-space (planned for the end of 2026), launch a first route between the University Hospital, the city hospitals and labs.
